purpose: Resolve the open question the red team opened: O-3's premise is measurably false, so does the enumerative escape it exposes actually yield sublinear candidate testing?
measured_by: dispatching session (Bash), coordinator-side - NOT independent validation
the_open_question: O-3 assumed >= 1 S-box per candidate. That premise is FALSE: distinct S-box computations over any key set are capped at 200 x 256 = 2^15.64, so per-candidate S-box work tends to zero for structured sets above dimension ~16. The question left open was whether the NON-S-box work - the linear layer and key addition - also amortizes. If it does, candidate testing is genuinely sublinear and the enumerative ceiling collapses. If it does not, O-3's conclusion survives on different grounds than it was argued on.
method: For affine cosets of the AES-128 master key at dimension d, with a fixed plaintext, count DISTINCT FULL 16-byte intermediate states entering each of the 10 rounds across the whole coset. Sharing of per-candidate work requires state collisions; fully distinct states mean each candidate needs its own computation chain.

measured.d8_set_size_256: 256 distinct states at every round 1-10, zero collisions
measured.d12_set_size_4096: 4096 distinct states at every round 1-10, zero collisions

resolution: NON-S-BOX WORK DOES NOT AMORTIZE. Full states are 128 bits and never collide across a structured key set, so every candidate requires its own linear-layer and key-addition work even though the byte-level S-box lookups saturate at 2^15.64 distinct values. The asymmetry is exactly explained: an S-box input is one byte and its space is exhausted by a few thousand keys, whereas the state is sixteen bytes and its space is not.
net_effect: O-3's PREMISE is false and its CONCLUSION survives, re-established on the correct grounds. The binding per-candidate cost is the state computation, not the S-box count. The 7.64-bit figure remains the wrong justification for the right bound; the right justification is that per-candidate state work is irreducible for structured sets, measured here to dimension 12.
not_established: Measured on affine master-key cosets at d = 8 and 12 only. Other structured families - last-round-key cosets pulled back through the schedule, sets closed under a byte-swap symmetry - are unmeasured, and the red team named them.

Absence of FULL-STATE collisions does not exclude PARTIAL sharing: a test that never forms the full state, working on a projection that does collide, is not excluded by this measurement. That is the residual form of the red team's F-1 and it remains open.
No claim about AES security. No impossibility claim. Nothing here is a break or progress toward one.
Coordinator-side; shares the campaign's single model under 0137a051; not independent validation.
